# Evidence comparison and focused search audit

NutriClinic · focused-audit record begun 24 October 2026; provenance addendum 25 October 2026, interface 0.3.5. This package documents focused primary-source verification, not an exhaustive systematic review or completed risk-of-bias assessment. Trial size, design, delivered exposure, endpoints and access are separated. Original full text through SBÜ VETİS was previously reviewed for EFFORT Protein, GLIM intake 2026, GLINTS 2026 and Deng 2026. New update records retain their actual open/full-text/abstract access labels. No institutional credentials or proxy URLs are included.

Türkçe: Bu kayıt hedefli taramayı ve erişim düzeyini açıklar; sistematik derleme tamamlandı iddiası taşımaz. Ana odak malnütrisyon, metabolik değerlendirme ve beslenme desteğidir. Özel bileşenler yalnız ilgili endikasyon bağlamında yorumlanır.

## 25 October provenance addendum / ENGINE ve PROMS yöntem eki

[ENGINE and Summers/PROMS source methods](ENGINE-SUMMERS-SOURCE-METHODS.md) consolidates the completed original-source audits with URLs, access limits, registry chronology and selected exact queries. **ENGINE NCT06238674:** the 78-person PCR analysis is nested in the 80-person parent, with two incomplete urine collections excluded. The combined randomized nutrition strategy is distinct from the exploratory achieved-intake association. Public registration followed the reported conduct interval; paper/registry start dates conflict. The PCR equation supplement remains unread. **PROMS ACTRN12620000776909:** preserve 29 randomized / 21 completed / 20 analysed and the separate registry final-20 field. Indexed original methods/results were read, without direct full-text/supplement access; registered whole-body balance/breakdown were not analysed and no prepublished SAP was available. Six-hour muscle synthesis cannot establish net balance or a daily dose.

These provenance additions concern **two existing records**: **62 catalog publications**, **12 selected lineage mappings**, no new independent cohort or unique-participant total. See [family mapping](STUDY-FAMILIES-AND-SCREENING.md). Earlier date-stamped audit sections below retain their scope; the updated Summers row and ENGINE access note incorporate this addendum. No new VETİS access was used for these two audits.

# ICU protein evidence comparison — focused primary-source audit

Audit date: **24 October 2026**. This is a focused update, not a systematic review or treatment recommendation. Existing `dist/evidence*.mjs`, `outputs/2026-ICU-EVIDENCE.md` and `outputs/RESEARCH-PROTOCOL.md` were read. Searches used exact study titles/DOIs and 2026 ICU protein/RCT terms, followed by original journal, PubMed, author-repository and official society sources. No VETİS/browser session was used by this auditor. Access below describes this audit only; it does not override independently documented institutional access.

## Comparison for the physician evidence screen

| Source and evidence tier | Population / phase / exposure | Main result and uncertainty | Interpretation and access |
|---|---|---|---|
| **EFFORT Protein (2023)** — original multicenter pragmatic RCT | 85 ICUs, 16 countries; 1,329 randomized/1,301 analyzed, ventilated nutritionally high-risk adults; intervention within 96 h. Prescription ≥2.2 versus ≤1.2 g/kg/day. Delivered mean 1.6±0.5 versus 0.9±0.3 g/kg/day is independently quoted in official ESPEN guidance. | Time to discharge alive by day 60: HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.77–1.07; p=0.27. 60-day mortality RR 1.08, 0.92–1.26. AKI/high-organ-failure harm signals are subgroup findings. | Does not establish benefit from the higher early prescription; it does not identify one optimal dose for every patient. **Original publisher abstract indexed and reviewed; direct full-text request returned 403.** [Original journal](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0140673622024692), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36708732/), DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(22)02469-2. |
| **PRECISe (2024)** — original blinded multicenter RCT | 935 ventilated adults; isocaloric enteral targets 2.0 versus 1.3 g/kg/day; delivered median 1.87 (IQR 0.96–2.00) versus 1.19 (0.63–1.26). | EQ-5D-5L through 180 days: mean difference −0.05, 95% CI −0.10 to −0.01; p=0.031. Death assigned zero in this endpoint. Overall mortality HR 1.14 (0.92–1.40), p=0.22. | Lower primary quality-of-life score does not mean proven mortality harm. Surviving-patient functional endpoints and exploratory subgroups require separate labels. **Original full paper opened in university repository**, methods/results/table 2 reviewed. [Repository and original PDF](https://orbi.uliege.be/handle/2268/328391), DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01304-7. |
| **TARGET Protein (2025)** — original cluster randomized crossover RCT | 3,397 adults, eight ICUs; isocaloric formula 100 versus 63 g protein/L. Median exposure 87 versus 84 h. | Days alive/free of index hospital at day 90: median difference −1.97 days, 95% CI −7.24 to 3.30; p=0.46. | Formula concentration is not delivered g/kg. Supplement 3 eTable 6 reports trial-formula contribution across all feeding days: 0.87 versus 0.53 g/kg **actual** weight/day; eTable 7 excluding enrollment day: 1.04 versus 0.64. These are not interchangeable total intake estimates. **Original journal full text and supplement opened.** [Journal, including Supplement 3](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2835302), DOI 10.1001/jama.2025.9110. |
| **Summers (2026), PROMS ACTRN12620000776909** — small mechanistic RCT | 29 randomized / 21 completed / 20 analysed, ten/group; current registry final 20 is a distinct field. Single intraduodenal whey dose 40 versus 20 g over 1 h; six-hour postprandial observation. | Muscle protein synthesis adjusted difference 0.007 %/h, 95% CI −0.003 to 0.016; p=0.152, despite greater amino acid availability. | Plasma leucine is not net muscle balance; nonsignificance is not equivalence. No daily dose or patient-centered efficacy rule. **Original indexed abstract plus publisher Methods/Results and current registry reviewed; direct full text/supplement not accessed.** Registered whole-body balance/breakdown were not analysed; no prepublished SAP available. [Original abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42085214/), DOI 10.1093/ajrccm/aamag086; [access/method audit](ENGINE-SUMMERS-SOURCE-METHODS.md). |
| **Deng (2026)** — original retrospective longitudinal cohort | MIMIC-IV n=5,370; ICU stay ≥7 days; supportive NEED cohort n=1,322; marginal structural Cox models. | Higher energy adequacy HR 0.61 (0.50–0.74), protein adequacy HR 0.51 (0.42–0.63) for 28-day mortality. Associations restricted to physiological strata. | Norepinephrine-equivalent <0.3 µg/kg/min and lactate <2 mmol/L; for protein, also creatinine <5 mg/dL. These are association strata, not validated dosing/start thresholds. Conditioning on ≥7-day stays and residual confounding limit causal use. **Original indexed PubMed abstract reviewed; full text not reviewed here.** The existing project separately documents a VETİS review. [Original abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42562321/), DOI 10.1016/j.clnesp.2026.105009. |
| **NEED age analysis (2026)** — exploratory post hoc analysis | n=2,672, 88 ICUs; parent enrollment 2018–2019. Tests protocolized feeding versus usual care, not isolated protein dose. | Mortality interaction HR ratio per ten years 1.28 (1.13–1.46); age ≤65 HR 0.64 (0.44–0.92), ≥76 HR 1.29 (0.89–1.88). | No multiplicity adjustment; authors call results hypothesis generating. This is not new 2026 randomization and does not justify withholding support by age. **Original open full text reviewed.** [Journal](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40560-026-00942-y), DOI 10.1186/s40560-026-00942-y. |

## What disagreement actually means

- **Guideline versus trial:** ESPEN 2023 already discusses EFFORT and states progressive delivery of 1.3 g/kg/day, Grade 0, 92% consensus. Thus it is inaccurate to suggest ESPEN was unaware of EFFORT. It predates PRECISe/TARGET and does not prove that 1.3 is optimal in every phase. [Official original guideline, recommendation 25 and commentary](https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_practical_and_partially_revised_guideline_Clinical_nutrition_in_the_intensive_care_unit.pdf).
- **An older range is not new proof:** the official ASPEN 2022 summary retained 1.2–2.0 g/kg/day because comparative protein evidence was insufficient then. Evidence date, strength and population should accompany that range. The accessed document was the official factsheet, **not the complete guideline**. [Official summary](https://nutritioncare.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Adult-Crit-Ill-Patient-Guidelines-Factsheet.pdf).
- **Observational association versus randomized contrast:** tolerating/delivering more food can be linked to being less ill. Adjustment reduces measured confounding; it does not make an observational threshold a randomized treatment rule. The studies also contrast different doses, time windows, routes and endpoints. Their estimates should not be averaged into a single bedside target.
- **Clinical phase and setting:** early ventilated ICU trials do not settle the effect of later rehabilitation, outpatient sarcopenia, burns, all neurological diagnoses, or KRT subgroups. Display the study’s population and phase before describing applicability.

## Additional primary records verified for the update module

The new `dist/evidence-update-20261024.mjs` contains succinct bilingual records with source-access distinctions for:

1. [Wulandari ICU BCAA](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clnesp.2025.11.153): positive small study; exposure confounding, attrition and surrogate outcomes remain visible.
2. [Veldsman AA plus mobilization](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12865756/): original methods accessible; combined intervention, not isolated amino-acid efficacy.
3. [ENGINE PCR post hoc analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42628743/): original indexed abstract plus publisher section snippets, parent Methods and official current registry checked in the 25 October addendum; complete 2026 text and PCR supplement unread. ENGINE NCT06238674 is a combined-strategy parent, not a validated PCR-guided individual dose trial. [Source/method audit](ENGINE-SUMMERS-SOURCE-METHODS.md).

Do not call all three newly conducted 2026 trials: the first two appeared online in late 2025 and in 2026 issues; the third reanalyzes existing randomization. None supplies an automatic supplementation rule.

## Verification and remaining gaps

- This search verified indexed 2026 records but does not establish exhaustive coverage through October 24. Search indexing and online/print dates differ; registration and a protocol are not outcome evidence.
- A 2026 enteral-protein meta-analysis surfaced (PMID 42048978), and a 2026 nutrition review (PMID 42418776). They are secondary material, not new participant randomization; no new study record was silently substituted from them.
- Direct PubMed HTML requests intermittently returned only a footer even when the indexed original abstract was available in search. Access logs therefore distinguish **indexed original abstract** from directly opened full text.
- For thesis-ready use, archive the exact search queries/date/results, dual-screen eligibility, reconcile trial registrations/supplements/corrections, and appraise risk of bias separately from sample size. No such completed systematic-review claim is made by this focused audit.
- Existing protocol section 10 still describes EFFORT as abstract-only, while the current evidence module and ICU note describe later VETİS access. Preserve time-stamped access history and reconcile that stale statement rather than silently assuming every document is current.

## Added source entry: NEXIS 2026

Root's exact focused query was `2026 critically ill protein amino acid randomized trial leucine BCAA mobilization`. It identified **NEXIS**, a multicenter phase 2 RCT, PMID 42438140, DOI 10.1093/ajrccm/aamag287. [Original PubMed abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42438140/) and the [original publisher abstract page](https://academic.oup.com/ajrccm/advance-article-abstract/doi/10.1093/ajrccm/aamag287/8732445) were checked. Online publication was **13 July 2026**, ahead of print; no print issue was verified. Full text was not reviewed. The fourth update-module record captures its combined intervention and neutral functional result with the wide confidence interval. This is new multicenter phase 2 evidence, not a large phase 3 confirmatory protein-only trial.

**25 October 2026 provenance update:** The original NEXIS abstract and [official current registry](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03021902) verify **NCT03021902**. Its [2019 protocol](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/9/7/e027893), DOI 10.1136/bmjopen-2018-027893, was accessible as indexed original passages; complete protocol/result methods and final SAP were not reviewed. Current registry neurological and AKI exclusions describe that record, not verified final 2026 cohort counts or automatic app eligibility rules. Protocol/registry/result documents do not create separate trials or participant totals. Details and access limits are in [HMB and NEXIS source methods](HMB-NEXIS-SOURCE-METHODS.md).

# Component and refeeding comparison audit

Research date: 24 October 2026 (Europe/Istanbul). Purpose: support a physician's documented interpretation of research; these comparisons must not set a dose, bypass a safety gate, or change the calculation engine. This is a targeted evidence audit, not a registered systematic review. Existing amino-acid and index records were read, then original publications and official guidelines were checked through public web access. No VETIS/browser session was used by this subagent. Access descriptions below refer to this audit, not earlier team access.

## 1. Supplemental glutamine: route and population are essential

| Original source | Population / regimen | Outcomes and uncertainty | Interpretation / limitations / access |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [REDOXS, NEJM 2013, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1212722](https://www.oeaie.org/content/uploads/2014/08/Heyland2013_A-Randomized-Trial-of-Glutamine-and-Antioxidants.pdf) | 1,223 ventilated adults with multiorgan failure, 40 ICUs. Blinded 2×2 factorial trial. Within 24 hours: supplemental IV glutamine 0.35 g/kg ideal body weight/day plus 30 g/day enteral glutamine, separate from nutrition. | 28-day mortality 32.4% versus 27.2%; adjusted OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.00–1.64; p=.05, above the prespecified final significance threshold .044. In-hospital and six-month mortality were significantly higher with glutamine. | Strong reason against treating biochemical rationale as an indication for this regimen. Combined early IV+enteral supplementation is not isolated enteral glutamine or ordinary formula protein. This was not exclusively a sepsis trial. Original article PDF opened; methods and outcomes inspected. |
| [RE-ENERGIZE, NEJM 2022, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2203364](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/295097/1/Re-Energize%20%28NEJM%2022%29%20.pdf) | 1,209 randomized, 1,200 analyzed severe-burn patients; double-blind international trial. Enteral glutamine 0.5 g/kg/day versus maltodextrin, started within 72 hours; protocol duration depended on grafting/discharge, capped at three months. | Time to live discharge: median 40 versus 38 days; subdistribution HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.80–1.04. Six-month mortality 17.2% versus 16.2%; HR 1.06, 0.80–1.41. | No demonstrated discharge/survival benefit. Not proof of equivalence or a sepsis/organ-failure safety trial. Renal dysfunction and cirrhosis were exclusions; sample size/primary endpoint changed during slow enrollment. Original university-hosted article PDF opened. |
| [Lee et al., 15 October 2026, DOI 10.4266/acc.002132](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42875940/) | Meta-analysis of ten IV glutamine RCTs, 1,593 adults; search updated April 2025. | Mortality RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.77–1.13; any infection RR 0.86, 0.63–1.18. Pneumonia RR 0.65, 0.49–0.87 and ventilation MD −0.97 days, −1.62 to −0.32 arose from few small trials. | New synthesis, not a new 2026 randomization. Heterogeneous regimens/populations, and secondary signals do not establish routine clinical benefit. Original PubMed abstract was read through its indexed record; full text was not obtained in this audit. |

**Legitimate comparison:** record whether the clinician is reviewing *additional* glutamine, its route, organ-failure/burn population, timing, and actual outcome sought. A research rationale can explain why routine extra supplementation is unsupported. A “REDOXS regimen” must not be offered as an executable alternative, and a burn subgroup must not be used to bypass organ-failure warnings. These are interpretation requirements inferred from the distinctions above.

[KSPEN 2026, R23](https://e-acnm.org/journal/view.php?doi=10.15747/ACNM.26.0059) recommends against routine enteral glutamine supplementation; its label is expert consensus with 95% agreement, not a quantified treatment effect. Publisher HTML and indexed recommendation text were accessible. This is compatible with declining routine supplementation; it does not imply all formulations/routes have identical risk.

## 2. Pure leucine, BCAA mixtures, protein products, and HMB are different interventions

| Original source | Population / regimen | Outcomes with reported CI | Why apparently conflicting findings are not interchangeable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [LACE 2022, DOI 10.1002/jcsm.12934](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcsm.12934) | 145 adults aged ≥70 with sarcopenia, 14 centers; double-blind 2×2 factorial design. Pure leucine 2.5 g three times daily versus lactose powder for 12 months; perindopril randomized separately. | Adjusted SPPB effect +0.1 points, 95% CI −1.0 to 1.1, p=.90; no demonstrated muscle-mass benefit. | Pure leucine was tested, not a protein/energy/vitamin mixture. Recruitment stopped early versus 440 planned; median adherence about 76%; wide uncertainty does not prove exact absence of benefit. Publisher full text opened; methods and outcome table inspected. |
| [PROVIDE 2015, DOI 10.1016/j.jamda.2015.05.021](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1525861015003886) | 380 primarily independent-living sarcopenic older adults, SPPB 4–9. Twice daily for 13 weeks: leucine/vitamin-D-enriched whey product versus isocaloric nonprotein control. Each serving included 20 g whey, 3 g total leucine, 800 IU vitamin D. | Co-primary handgrip/SPPB between-group benefits were not significant. Secondary appendicular mass +0.17 kg, 95% CI 0.004–0.338; chair-stand time −1.01 seconds, −1.77 to −0.19. | Multicomponent and not nitrogen matched: improvement cannot be assigned to leucine alone. Short follow-up and secondary endpoints matter. Sponsor involvement disclosed. Publisher original abstract indexed/read; university full-text PDF returned 403. Composition corroborated in the [original PROVIDE follow-up methods](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6583678/); full primary protocol/supplement still merits VETIS verification. |
| [Chan et al., August 2026, DOI 10.3390/life16081334](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13514121/) | Single-center sarcopenia/presarcopenia, age ≥65. 80 randomized, 73 completers analyzed over eight weeks. Daily mixture: 3 g leucine / 6 g total BCAA, 10 g whey, 6 g MCT, 5 g creatine, 400 IU D3, 50 mg resveratrol; 160 kcal, isocaloric maltodextrin control. | DXA appendicular mass difference +0.45 kg, 95% CI 0.15–0.75. Grip +0.62 kg, −0.62 to 1.86; gait speed −0.03 m/s, −0.15 to 0.10. | Not an ICU trial or isolated leucine effect. Completer analysis, differential losses 6/1, retrospective registration, no measured diet/activity, short duration. Abstract calls 73 randomized while methods show 80. PMC full text and indexed tables were reviewed; subsequent requests intermittently reached bot checks, MDPI returned 429. |
| [Sunsandee et al. 2025, DOI 10.1007/s11255-025-04560-9](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11255-025-04560-9) | 55 CKD patients aged >65; 29 versus 26. Twelve weeks of leucine-enriched BCAA: 4.5 g leucine, 1.5 g valine, 1.5 g isoleucine/day versus placebo. | Lean-mass changes +0.4 kg (95% CI 0.1–0.7) versus −0.2 kg (−0.6 to 0.2), p=.010. These are arm-specific change CIs, **not** the between-group effect CI. No demonstrated strength/functional benefit. | CKD-specific small trial; no basis for automatic renal supplementation. Similar reported energy/protein intake does not establish nitrogen-matched design. Publisher abstract accessible, full text subscription-only; placebo, CKD stage, missing data and safety exclusions need full-text review. |
| [Wu et al. 2025, DOI 10.1186/s13054-025-05660-9](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13054-025-05660-9) | 266 adults across **10 ICUs in 5 hospitals**, open-label 2×2 factorial trial with blinded outcome assessment. The cohort includes **112 participants from the earlier 2023 report** under the same registration, ChiCTR2200057685. Calcium HMB 1.5 g twice daily orally/enterally; resistance training was a separate factor. | HMB discharge SPPB difference +0.282 points, 95% CI −0.599 to 1.162; six-minute walk +10.170 m, −22.450 to 42.788. | Resistance-training findings cannot be assigned to HMB; no functional benefit demonstrated for HMB itself. No matching placebo, variable exposure/follow-up. Neuro-ICU generalization is limited by the eligibility criteria. Original full text inspected; the 112 earlier participants must not be added again as an independent cohort. |
| [Berger et al., July 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.clnu.2026.106690](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0261561426001172) | Secondary post hoc analysis of the Lausanne HMB-ICU-CH trial, **NCT03628365**; 37 included. Parent report: Viana 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.clnu.2021.07.018. HMB 3 g/day versus placebo, ≥10 days; isotope/biochemical assessment on ICU days 4 and 15. | Reported UCR contrast 125 versus 181, p=.002. **Analyte/unit basis remains unverified**; it is not interchangeable with the app's mg/dL-based urea/creatinine or BUN/creatinine outputs. Indexed Discussion describes a smaller increase; no verified within-person fall or contrast CI is inferred. | Exploratory biochemical findings do not establish anti-inflammatory or functional benefit, survival improvement, an anabolic target or an optimal dose. Original abstract and indexed publisher Methods reviewed; direct full-text access 403, complete tables not reviewed. This is a later report of an existing randomization, with overlapping participants. See [source-method audit](HMB-NEXIS-SOURCE-METHODS.md). |

**Legitimate comparison:** a physician may document whether an energy/protein gap justifies a verified oral product and whether its population matches the patient. The display should compare whole intervention compositions, co-interventions and function versus mass endpoints. “Pure leucine works” is not supported by a positive multicomponent mass endpoint. “HMB lowers a blood ratio” is not a reason to declare anabolism or automatically select HMB. No optimal dose or relative ranking among these supplements can be inferred from these non-head-to-head trials.

## 3. Refeeding: genuine guideline disagreement plus different populations/definitions

These are published approaches for comparison, not selectable dosing shortcuts. The physician's documentation should identify the institutional protocol/version, prevention versus developed syndrome, care setting, electrolyte trend, thiamine, monitoring capacity, and justification. Retain the existing engine's risk/safety blocks.

| Authoritative source | Published approach and setting | Interpretation boundary / access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [NICE CG32, 1.4.6–1.4.8](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/recommendations) | High-risk adults: start at no more than 10 kcal/kg/day, advance to full needs over 4–7 days. Extreme cases, e.g. BMI <14 or negligible intake >15 days: 5 kcal/kg/day and continuous rhythm monitoring. Close fluid/clinical monitoring; thiamine 200–300 mg/day before/during first ten days. | A preventive high-risk protocol, not evidence that every low phosphate is developed syndrome. Original official indexed recommendations were read; direct HTML/PDF requests were blocked (403). Clinical update is 2017; a 2026 footer is not a new guideline version. |
| [ASPEN 2020, Table 6](https://aspenjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ncp.10474) | At-risk adults: 10–20 kcal/kg in first 24 hours or 100–150 g dextrose, advancing about 33% of goal every 1–2 days. Include enteral/parenteral glucose and IV dextrose. Baseline P/K/Mg; high-risk monitoring every 12 hours for first three days. Severe low P/K/Mg: delay initiation/increase until corrected. | Consensus with acknowledged limited controlled data; special populations such as renal impairment require adaptation. Definition of developed syndrome uses P/K/Mg decline over five days, with severity/organ-dysfunction criteria. Publisher full text and adult table read; correction DOI 10.1002/ncp.10491 should accompany implementation. |
| [AuSPEN 2025, especially sections 3.5.1–3.5.2](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5a963e1a1137a60b45455f0c/t/68366c5a6b553145a61b8c85/1748397150638/AuSPEN%2BConsensus%2Bstatements%2Bon%2Brefeeding%2Bsyndrome.pdf) | General adult inpatients: commence at ≥50% of estimated requirements and reach goal in 24–72 hours, with close clinical/electrolyte monitoring. Its diagnosis requires adequate intake, electrolyte changes and clinical symptoms, not electrolyte decline alone. | **The ICU section explicitly retains existing conservative critical-care feeding guidance.** Rapid general-inpatient advancement is not a competing full-feeding ICU protocol. High-quality critical-care data are inadequate; hypophosphatemia has other causes. Many statements rely on low-level evidence/expert opinion. Official 28-page PDF opened; relevant initiation/ICU sections inspected. |
| [KSPEN 2026, R42–R45](https://e-acnm.org/journal/view.php?doi=10.15747/ACNM.26.0059) | Critically ill adults: screen after ICU admission, assess/replete P/K/Mg before and during early therapy, thiamine before nutrition. R44 suggests 100–150 g glucose or 10–20 kcal/kg first 24 hours, gradual advancement every 1–2 days. | Expert consensus, 97% agreement for R44; not a new efficacy trial or automatic individual prescription. This 2026 ICU recommendation aligns with cautious initiation rather than importing general AuSPEN escalation into every ICU patient. Publisher/indexed recommendation text accessible. |

Two original trials explain why a binary “slow versus fast” evidence label is misleading:

- [Doig et al. 2015, DOI 10.1016/S2213-2600(15)00418-X](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26597128/): 339 adults at 13 ICUs **after** refeeding-associated hypophosphatemia developed within 72 hours. Protocolized restriction versus continued standard support: primary days alive after ICU discharge +4.9 days, 95% CI −2.3 to 13.6, p=.19; day-60 survival was a favorable component (91% versus 78%, p=.002). Not proof of a preventive dose for all at-risk adults. Original abstract read; complete trial protocol not accessed. Avoid converting the secondary/component result into an unqualified positive primary trial.
- [Ambrose et al. 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.clnesp.2020.11.028](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405457720311062): ward-based PN referrals at moderate/high risk, very-high-risk exclusions; 100% versus 50% requirements during first 48 hours. Early termination; 104 risk-stratified, 97 analyzed overall, only 48 had primary-outcome data. No detected difference in refeeding indicators (p>.99); not demonstrated noninferiority/equivalence. The indexed abstract's low-arm unit reads “15 kcal/day” whereas its design describes 50% of needs: verify the original protocol before extracting a numeric dose. Publisher preview/indexed methods read; Oxford full-text link returned 403. No primary between-arm CI available in the accessed abstract.

## Implementation conclusions (audit interpretation)

1. Display supported and unsupported **interpretations**, not “choose your preferred result.” Allow a physician to record a considered approach only as research documentation with sources and limitations visible. Acknowledgment does not make an unsupported intervention equally recommended.
2. Refeeding documentation can name the institution-approved guideline and explain population fit; no toggle should import one guideline's starts, another's risk criteria, and a third's diagnosis as a validated hybrid.
3. Store the exact reviewed inputs, choice/rationale, cited records, and time. A material input change invalidates acknowledgment. Keep dose calculations, source product composition and raw patient data separate from this review.
4. Do not display invented GRADE, RoB2 scores, a universal efficacy rank, or computed CIs from only arm-specific published CIs. Structured critical appraisal can record the observed design facts above; formal ratings need a separately documented assessment process.

## Search limits / 2026 update

Searches targeted original glutamine/leucine/BCAA/HMB trials and refeeding guidance through 24 October 2026 using PubMed, publisher pages, official society/NICE material and primary university repositories. 2026 priority yielded the glutamine synthesis, KSPEN recommendations, small TLN-01 trial and HMB post hoc analysis. None establishes a new universally optimal supplement or refeeding dose. No new large, directly applicable 2026 head-to-head RCT was identified in this bounded search; this is not proof that none exists. Embase/CENTRAL were not independently searched, supplements/registries were not fully audited, and subscription originals listed above still require VETIS review. Conference-only multi-ingredient/digital-coaching abstracts were not used as clinical efficacy foundations. No existing repository files were changed for this audit.

# Function and dysphagia criteria audit

Cutoff: 24 October 2026, Europe/Istanbul. This targeted audit checked original/official sources for EWGSOP2, EAT-10, FOIS and IDDSI, plus 2025–2026 changes relevant to a neurologist. It does not establish clinical validation of NutriClinic. This subagent used public web/publisher access, not VETIS; source-access limits below must not be presented as institutional full-text review.

## What the module implements

`dist/criteria-function.mjs` exports `evaluateFunction(input, measures)` and bilingual `functionSources`. It returns five source-linked bilingual records with `id`, `title`, `status`, `summary`, `details`, `values`, and `sourceIds`. IDs are `ewgsop2`, `eat10`, `fois`, `iddsi`, and `swallow-safety`.

The function never sets an energy/protein dose, orders a tube, recommends a thickener/texture, authorizes oral feeding, or offers a water challenge. It does not modify the existing clinical engine. Numeric input must be a finite number; unfilled fields are unknown. Source, a real assessment date no later than the visit date, and explicit clinician confirmation are required for interpreted records.

### Sarcopenia

The module records the low-strength/low-muscle-quantity/performance pattern and calls it a **candidate**, not a diagnosis. It preserves the distinction between appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM), ASM/height², total lean mass and FFMI. ICU context or declared confounding prevents a classified candidate output; low numerical results remain available for specialist interpretation. Neurological weakness, sedation, pain, inability to cooperate and fluid shifts require clinical interpretation rather than attribution to primary age-related sarcopenia. This context restriction is a software safeguard, not a claim that EWGSOP2 excludes every acute/secondary case.

### Swallowing

EAT-10 is a symptom score; ≥3 raises a symptom-review flag. Low/zero scores never establish absence of silent aspiration. FOIS is a clinician-entered functional intake record. IDDSI food (3–7) and fluid (0–4) levels are separate clinician records. They are neither inferred from EAT-10 nor converted into orders. A recorded FOIS 1 conflicts with an oral route and prompts reconciliation without selecting a replacement route.

`swallow-safety.values.hasUnsafeSwallow` is true for explicit unsafe swallow, impaired alertness, or reported unsafe signs, even if EAT-10 is zero or documentation is incomplete. `safetyReasons` contains machine IDs. Missing/unverified information does not create safety clearance. FEES/VFSS are described as clinician-selected instrumental options; impaired consciousness/cooperation requires suitability assessment and may contraindicate FEES. The app offers no water or food challenge.

## Original and official sources

### EWGSOP2 and its correction

[Cruz-Jentoft et al., Age and Ageing 2019; DOI 10.1093/ageing/afy169](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6322506/) supplies strength, quantity and performance criteria. Numerical implementation: grip <27 kg men/<16 women or five chair rises >15 seconds; ASM <20 kg men/<15 women, or ASM/height² <7/<5.5 kg/m²; gait ≤0.8 m/s or SPPB ≤8. The thresholds use the appropriate European/population context.

The [official 2019 correction, DOI 10.1093/ageing/afz046](https://academic.oup.com/ageing/article/48/4/601/5488778) changes the female ASM/height² cutoff from the erroneous <6.0 to **<5.5 kg/m²**. Some accepted-manuscript/indexed versions still show 6.0; they must not control the implementation.

Access: original indexed text/table and publisher correction text were read; direct PMC calls intermittently reached bot checks and direct Oxford article calls redirected to inaccessible CDN endpoints. No full article reproduction is bundled. The primary article's CC BY-NC terms should not be treated as an unrestricted commercial license; the module contains numeric factual thresholds and original implementation wording.

### EAT-10 original and validated Turkish adaptation

[Belafsky et al. 2008, DOI 10.1177/000348940811701210](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19140539/) reports the original prospective instrument development/validation: 629 surveys in 482 patients; normative data support an abnormal total ≥3. The score is a self-reported symptom/outcome instrument, not an instrumental airway-protection test. Access: original PubMed/publisher indexed abstract read; direct PubMed returned a minimal footer and publisher full-text access timed out.

[Demir et al. 2016, Turkish EAT-10, DOI 10.1007/s00455-016-9723-9](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27405421/) evaluated 105 patients. Participants completed the instrument without assistance; reported internal consistency was .90/.91. This supports using the validated Turkish form, not translating English item text ad hoc inside the app. Access: original indexed abstract and [author institution record](https://research.hacettepe.edu.tr/en/publications/reliability-and-validity-of-the-turkish-eating-assessment-tool-t--2/) read; full methods/form were not obtained.

Copyright handling: no blanket license to reproduce/translate the questionnaire items was verified. Therefore the UI should accept a clinician-entered total from the original validated form. The helper can sum ten numeric scores copied from an authorized external form but contains **no question/item wording**. Partially answered items are not assigned zero; inconsistent entered total versus item sum requires reconciliation. Neither EAT-10 item text nor a new translated questionnaire is supplied.

### FOIS original

[Crary, Carnaby Mann and Groher 2005, DOI 10.1016/j.apmr.2004.11.049](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0003999305001966) evaluated a seven-point ordinal functional oral-intake record in a 302-patient acute stroke cohort, including change over six months. Its purpose is to document intake function, not to directly classify aspiration physiology. Original indexed abstract/method description were read; a complete authorized scale-reproduction license was not verified. The module stores a clinician-selected integer 1–7 with original explanatory text; it does not reproduce the scale's full level-descriptor table or create new labels that claim scale validation.

### IDDSI official standard and actual 2026 update

[IDDSI official framework page](https://www.iddsi.org/standards/framework) separates drink levels 0–4 and food levels 3–7; product testing describes consistency under serving conditions, while patient recommendations remain the clinician's responsibility. The [official framework document/version page](https://www.iddsi.org/resources/framework-documents) states current detailed definitions **2.2** and testing methods **2.0**, including English and Turkish listings. The [official 2026 refresh notice](https://www.iddsi.org/) describes April 2026 changes to certain examples/images. This is a real version update, not a new aspiration prediction score.

Access: official indexed pages read; direct HTML returned 403. The actual downloadable 2.2 files were not fetched in this audit, so no claim of page-by-page PDF inspection is made. The official standard's indexed notice specifies CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution and says not to alter framework elements beyond language translation. No framework image, pyramid, testing diagram, or adapted full framework is bundled. The module stores factual numeric domains and links to the official current documents; it does not declare that a formula has passed IDDSI product testing.

### 2025 instrumental assessment guidance

[UEG/ESNM clinical recommendations 2025, DOI 10.1002/ueg2.70062](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12269739/) statements 3.11–3.13 distinguish clinical assessment from instrumental characterization. Bedside evaluation alone is insufficient to fully characterize oropharyngeal dysfunction; FEES/VFSS are instrumental options with different clinical advantages. Statement 3.12 lists impaired consciousness among FEES contraindications and poor cooperation/agitation among relative limitations. Therefore “unsafe alertness → automatic FEES” would be an inappropriate software rule.

Access: original indexed statement text and university-hosted original guideline indexing were read; direct PMC reached a bot check and direct university PDF returned 403. Do not describe this as a full-text VETIS review. The module paraphrases boundaries without reproducing the guideline table or assigning new GRADE/RoB ratings.

### 2026 DIGEST–IDDSI mapping

[Hutcheson et al. 2026, DOI 10.1007/s00455-026-10943-6](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00455-026-10943-6) is a commentary mapping existing DIGEST bolus terminology to IDDSI. The authors explicitly say it does not change the method requiring new psychometric testing, and identify IDDSI levels 1, 5 and 6 as untested within DIGEST. It is not a newly validated global swallowing screen and cannot justify adding an automatic DIGEST grade from bedside data. Access: publisher full text read. Its CC BY-NC-ND license does not authorize distributing an adapted decision-tree graphic; none is reproduced.

### Other 2026 validation located but not adopted as a replacement

[Slovenian EAT-10 adaptation, DOI 10.1080/09638288.2026.2725142](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/09638288.2026.2725142) is a language-specific validation. Publisher indexed text was available, direct full text returned 403. A newer translation date does not supersede the original English or validated Turkish form. No new Turkish/English universal cutoff replacement was verified in this bounded search.

## Limits and verification

This was a focused public-source search, not a systematic review across Embase/CINAHL/CENTRAL or all disease-specific neurological cohorts. Instrument reliability/validity does not validate application performance in sedated neuro-ICU patients, people unable to self-report, or every aphasia/cognitive state. The function deliberately retains assessment validity and confounding fields and issues candidate/review outputs. Research source access is labeled honestly; full originals/forms and local protocols should be checked through the team's VETIS session where available.

Fifteen meaningful new tests cover threshold boundaries, corrected female indexing, ASM/FFMI separation, ICU/neuro confounding, missing and invalid values, EAT-10 symptom/aspiration distinction, partial/conflicting responses, source/date checks, FOIS versus route orders, IDDSI domains, unsafe alertness despite a zero score, bilingual/source integrity, and unchanged inputs. Only new module/test/audit files were created for this task.
